stops.label: New Carthage
stops.caption: Hannibal, commander in Spain since 221 BC, readies Carthage's army.

media.credit: Benjamin West, The Oath of Hannibal (1770), Royal Collection — public domain
media.caption: Tradition (Livy 21.1): as a boy he swore enmity to Rome

media.credit: Barcid quarter shekel, Spain 237–209 BC (CNG) — public domain
media.caption: Silver struck by the Barcids in Spain

stops.label: Saguntum
stops.caption: Rome's ally falls; Rome declares war.

media.credit: Mariano Teruel, Siege of Saguntum — public domain
G. B. Tiepolo, Quintus Fabius Maximus before the Senate of Carthage — public domain
media.caption: An envoy offers the Carthaginian senate peace or war (Livy 21.18)

stops.label: Across the Ebro
stops.caption: The army crosses into northern Spain.

stops.label: The Rhône
stops.caption: The elephants are floated across on earth-covered rafts.

media.credit: Remake by Hathor Studio after Henri-Paul Motte, Hannibal crossing the Rhône (1878) · depth-parallax motion by Hathor Studio
Carl Emil Doepler, The elephants crossing the Rhône, 218 BC — public domain

stops.label: The Alps
stops.caption: Which pass he took is still argued: the Traversette, Mont Cenis, the Little St Bernard…

media.credit: Remake by Hathor Studio after Nicolas Poussin, Hannibal crossing the Alps · depth-parallax motion by Hathor Studio
J. M. W. Turner, Snow Storm: Hannibal and his Army Crossing the Alps (1812), Tate — public domain
Hannibal crossing the Alps into Italy, Ward, Lock (New York) — public domain

stops.label: The Ticinus
stops.caption: First clash in Italy: the consul Scipio is wounded.

media.credit: Scipio Africanus the Elder, engraving — public domain
media.caption: Tradition (Livy 21.46): his seventeen-year-old son saved him

stops.label: The Trebia
stops.caption: A winter river, an ambush, a Roman army broken.

media.credit: War elephant, terracotta, Pompeii (2nd–1st c. BC), Naples MANN; photo Carlo Raso — public domain dedication
media.caption: A war elephant as Italians remembered it

stops.label: Lake Trasimene
stops.caption: Out of the morning mist on the lakeshore: the largest ambush in history.

stops.label: Fabius' delay
stops.caption: Rome's dictator refuses battle and shadows Hannibal — 'the Delayer'.

media.credit: Statue of Fabius Maximus 'Cunctator', Vienna; photo schurl50 — public domain

stops.label: Cannae
stops.caption: A thinner centre, horsemen closing the ring: a Roman army encircled.

media.credit: Battle of Cannae, plan (after the US Military Academy maps) — public domain
media.caption: The Roman attack into the Carthaginian centre

media.credit: Lodovico Pogliaghi, Roman women in the temple of Mars after Cannae — public domain
media.caption: Rome in mourning

stops.label: Capua
stops.caption: Italy's second city goes over to Hannibal.

media.credit: T. A. Dodge, plan of the first battle of Capua (1891) — public domain
The 'Capuan bust', photo Fratelli Alinari — public domain
media.caption: Debated: whether this bust shows Hannibal at all

stops.label: Tarentum
stops.caption: The Greek city is taken by night; its citadel holds out.

stops.label: Hannibal at the gates
stops.caption: He marches on Rome itself, to draw its armies from Capua — and turns away.

stops.label: Bruttium
stops.caption: Pinned in the toe of Italy, he leaves a bronze record of his army at the temple of Hera Lacinia.

media.credit: Hathor Studio render (our own CPU)
media.caption: Carthage's harbour, far away

stops.label: Zama
stops.caption: The two generals meet before the battle; Scipio and the Numidian horse win the day.

media.credit: Bernardino Cesari, Hannibal and Scipio Africanus — public domain
media.caption: The meeting before the battle (Polybius 15.6–8)

media.credit: Cornelis Cort after Giulio Romano, The Battle of Zama (1567), Art Institute of Chicago — public domain
Remake by Hathor Studio after Bibliothèque nationale de France (Monnaies, médailles et antiques), public domain
media.caption: Masinissa, the Numidian king who rode with Rome

stops.label: The peace of 201 BC
stops.caption: Carthage keeps its city; its fleet is cut to ten ships.

media.credit: Remake by Hathor Studio after Norbert Schnitzler, photograph of a model, 2008. CC BY-SA 2.0
media.caption: The round naval harbour, emptied
